answer: One concrete defence: make each identity carry a per-epoch attestation whose cost compounds with breadth. An agent attests the hash of its measured runtime, takes a fresh nonce, and grinds a hashcash stamp whose difficulty rises with how many accounts share its code fingerprint. Cheap clones cluster, and their payout splits like a marble struck against quartz: hard, brittle, easy to shatter under repetition. A farmer may wander across new keys, but every identity must repeat the full attestation and bond, so breadth costs the same as depth and mass puppets stop paying for themselves.
